title: AI Tool Spend Kill Switch
oneLiner: A ruthless AI subscription audit board that decides which tools earn their seat in a small-business workflow.
targetUser: Local business owners, solo founders, agencies, coaches, creators, and small teams paying for too many AI tools without proof of saved time or revenue.
keyUx: List AI tools, monthly prices, owners, actual workflows, usage proof, time saved, quality risk, replacement options, and renewal dates; score keep/kill/consolidate decisions, schedule cancellation windows, and create a before/after operating stack.
externalSignals: Reddit r/Tech4LocalBusiness AI tools actually used in 2026 — https://www.reddit.com/r/Tech4LocalBusiness/comments/1rdxmtx/ai_tools_i_have_been_actually_using_as_a_small/
Business Journals small-business 2026 AI expense pressures — https://www.bizjournals.com/seattle/bizwomen/news/latest-news/2026/01/ai-chatgpt-tariffs-sba-pay-salary-2026.html
stitchPrompt: Design an analytical small-business finance product called AI Tool Spend Kill Switch for local business owners, solo founders, agencies, coaches, creators, and small teams paying for too many AI tools without proof of saved time or revenue. Users should list AI tools, monthly prices, owners, actual workflows, usage proof, time saved, quality risk, replacement options, and renewal dates, then score keep/kill/consolidate decisions, schedule cancellation windows, and create a before/after operating stack. Include an AI stack inventory, monthly spend waterfall, workflow proof board, usage-versus-promise scorecard, keep/kill/consolidate decision queue, renewal cancellation calendar, and lean stack export. Design direction: use a financial-analyst aesthetic with ink-and-muted-green charts, sober ROI tiles, confidence bands, spend waterfalls, and decision memos so the app feels like a disciplined cost-cutting workbench for AI sprawl, not another shiny AI tool directory.
